Cyberpunk 2077 succeeded in creating one of the best worlds I’ve ever seen in any video game. Night City is rich and dark, fun and scary at the same time, with so much to do and countless secrets waiting to be discovered. The way everything unfolds in the city feels incredibly immersive.

The base game had some issues. The main story was good, but it felt somewhat lacking at times, and I felt the same way about some of the side quests. Phantom Liberty fixed most of my issues with the game.
It delivers an amazing story with complex characters, well-written side quests, and plenty of activities to do.

I really enjoyed my time in Cyberpunk 2077 and learned a lot throughout the experience. I’ll definitely miss its characters, atmosphere, and everything Night City has to offer.
Plays much smoother than my first play though and just as amazing. Can never get enough of this classic.

This game's early 2d platforming is INCREDIBLY reminiscent of the gameplay of the original Robocop on NES; spoken as someone who spent $45 in 1988 lawnmowing money ($127 adjusted for 2026) to get that NES cart.  I'm loving the T2 pixel art of Ed, Furlong et al and I'm only 20 minutes in.  I'm looking forward to outrunning an 18-wheeler on a motorbike,

11/10 stars, makes my soul ache to be out in the north woods again, and the idle mode is absolutely lovely to put on while you're doing other things. Every time I hook something big in idle mode it's like watching my own personal fishing tournament! If you like pixel art, nature sounds, creature collecting, and chill vibes, this one is a no-brainer.

This game had high praise on release so I was excited to try it out. It unfrotunately did not live up to my expectations. This game feels 'almost good' or 'almost fun'. The Devs strugle with their idea of balancing and making the game actually fun to play and from my persepective there are too many instances they don't succeed. There are so many mechanics that feel frustrating to use, reloading your gun, 90% of guns feel useless, new tank can't turn it's turret etc. Max level difficulty is inconsistent, sometimes challenging sometimes easy. Maps and terrain feel repetetive, flat and uninteresting to play on, verticality in movement and map design is barely explored.

Golf With Your Friends is simple mini-golf with friends, and that is mostly enough. You putt through themed courses, the ball physics are easy to read, and up to 12 people can pile into a lobby. Custom courses and the workshop keep it from getting stale if your group likes building or downloading maps.

Power-ups and the race modes add chaos when a normal round feels too quiet. The base courses are fine, not amazing, and the skill ceiling is low once everyone knows the holes. It is at its best as a warm-up or a late-night filler, not a main game.

Cheap, easy to jump into, and still fun after a few years if you already have people to play with. Solo or with randoms it does not hold up nearly as well.

This game pretty quick, but really fun. Crawling through the rooms as a monster and tearing through everything in your way is just fun. The map is pretty straight forward on where your supposed to go, so you won't get lost often. My first playthrough took around 6-8 hours, so the game goes pretty quick. I found it fun to come back to after a while though, so the game still has some replayability even after you beat it. Overall, really fun game and would highly recommend if you like quick games or horror/monster games.

A tiny, silly point and click that's way more replayable than you'd expect.

The more you play around with it, the more ways you find to untangle the little stories inside it. Love the art and visual style, is charming. It's a simple point and click at its core, but a really enjoyable one. You can mess around and see how many different ways you can solve a task or recruit companions along the way.

Great pick if you like short, quirky adventures with a lot of room to mess around and experiment.

I am coming back to this game after 4-5 years and (DESPITE IT'S ANNOYING WAY OF HANDLING DIFFICULTY), it has some of the smoothest platforming I have ever played. The visuals are absolutely phenomenal, and the soundtrack is practically transcendent. Although its runtime is incredibly short, it is worth each and every second of your time. The abilities feel smooth and responsive, each one goes together near perfectly, and even when you only have a third of them, you still feel like you're one with the character once you get the hang of the movement.

TL:DR: Phenomenal game all around, but do be aware that the later areas end up feeling more tedious and annoying than actually difficult (I'm looking at you, Sorrow Pass).

No, I’m Not a Human, is one of the best unsettling narratives I’ve ever experienced. This game is the ultimate test of morals, ethics, and seeing how people around you go about tough and unnerving situations. From watching people play this online, to introducing my friends to it in person, it has been amazing. There are so many things to discover, dialogue to read, emotions to feel, and endings to obtain. This is very much a reading game, and even if that isn’t your thing I would recommend giving it a try. The music is eerily peaceful, like a lure into bed after a long day, it draws you in and makes you feel calm, but also not fully able to relax. One of the best horror games I’ve played ever, and there is so much creative art and storytelling for each character having their own personalities and none of them being the same. Amazing work; for sure will be getting their next game!
